topic_title: Solving Systems of Linear Equations Using Elimination: One Transformation
value:
Notice that the coefficient of $s$ in the first equation is $-2$, while in the second equation it is $1$.

If we multiply the second equation by ${\color{blue}2}$, then the coefficient of $s$ will turn into $2$, which will cancel with the coefficient of $-2$ in the first equation.

$$
\{-2s - 5t = -4; (s - t = 7)\cdot (2)
$$

Now, when we add the two equations, the variable $s$ will be eliminated:

$$
\begin{aligned}
-2s - 5t &= -4 \\
2s - 2t &= 14 \\
(-5t - 2t) &= (-4 + 14) \\
-7t &= 10
\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is the following:

> *To eliminate $s$, multiply the $\bbox[3pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}\text{second}}$ equation by $\bbox[3pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}2}$, and add the equations*.
